TradeDate—Settlement Date Schedule

Overview

Pursuant to Sections 220.8(b)(1) and (4) of Regulation T of the Federal Reserve Board, a broker-dealer must promptly cancel or otherwise liquidate a customer purchase transaction in a cash account if full payment is not received within five business days from the date of purchase or, pursuant to Section 220.8(d)(1), make application to extend the time period specified. The date by which members must take such action is shown below in the column titled “Reg. T Date.”

Similarly, SEC Rule 15c3-3 requires member organizations to take prompt steps to obtain possession or control of securities pursuant to paragraph (m) through a buy-in procedure or otherwise if securities are not received within 13 business days from the date of sale or, pursuant to paragraph (n), make application to extend the time period specified. The date by which members must take such action is shown below in the column titled “SEC Extension Date.”

Brokers, dealers and municipal securities dealers should use the settlement dates for purposes of clearing and settling transactions pursuant to the securities exchanges.

            </p>
            <p><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">To meet rising demand for U.S. equities across the globe, Nasdaq is engaging with regulators to offer nearly continuous trading 23 hours a day, 5 days a week, on the Nasdaq Stock Market. On December 6, 2026, Nasdaq will introduce a new trading session from 9 p.m. to 4 a.m. ET.</font></p>
            <p><strong><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Order Handling</font></strong></p>
            <ul style="list-style-type: disc;">
                <li><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Members will need new order entry ports. </font></li>
                <li><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Routable orders will be accepted. </font></li>
                <li><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Any orders remaining open at 4 a.m. ET will be cancelled and can be re-entered in the subsequent session.</font></li>
            </ul>
            <p><strong><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Trade Date and Settlement</font></strong></p>
            <ul style="list-style-type: disc;">
                <li><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Trades executed between 9 p.m. ET and midnight will be assigned the next trading day's trade date.</font></li>
                <li><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Trades executed from midnight through 8 p.m. ET will carry the current day’s trade date.</font></li>
                <li><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Settlement processing will continue to be based on trade date. </font></li>
            </ul>
            <p><strong><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Market Protections</font></strong></p>
            <p><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Nasdaq will make Equities Risk Checks available through both API and WorkX.  In addition, the SEC has now approved a LULD national market system plan amendment requiring, among other things, the exchange’s rejection of orders priced outside certain static price bands disseminated via the securities information processors (SIPs). These bands will be based on the listing market's adjusted Official Closing Price and the adjusted last round-lot sale prior to 7:45 p.m. ET. The proposed upper band will be set 20% above the greater of the two reference prices, while the lower band will be set 20% below the lesser reference price, subject to minimum band widths of $3.00 for securities priced at or above $1.00 and $1.00 for securities priced below $1.00.</font></p>
            <p><strong><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Corporate Actions and Dividends</font></strong></p>
            <p><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">As described in the Exchange’s rule proposal to become operative on December 6, 2026, certain categories of corporate actions will be halted before 9 p.m. ET on the day immediately preceding the effective date and resumed at 8 a.m. ET on the effective date. Nasdaq will send a Trade Halt Code of ‘M1’ to denote Corporate Action. More information can be found in the </font><a href="https://www.nasdaq.com/docs/global-trading-hours-corporate-actions-faqs"><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Corporate Actions FAQ</font></a><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">.</font></p>

            <p><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Nasdaq Test Facility (NTF)</font></p>
            <ul style="list-style-type: disc;">
                <li><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif"></font><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">September 1, 2026</font></li>
            </ul>
            <p>Weekend User Acceptance Test (UAT) Schedule</p>
            <ul style="font-size: 12px;">
                <li><font style="font-size: 10pt;">October 2, 2026</font></li>
                <li><font style="font-size: 10pt;">October 16, 2026</font></li>

            <p><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Pre-Production Period</font></p>

            </ul>
            <p><font style="font-size: 10pt;" face=""Segoe UI", sans-serif">Order entry and trading of Nasdaq Test Symbols (ZXZZT, ZVZZT, and ZWZZT) will be available between 9 p.m. and 4 a.m. Market data will be broadcast for Nasdaq Test Symbols during the pre-production period.</font></p>

Extended Hours Trading

There are also pre-market and after hours trading sessions available, also known as Extended Markets. For Nasdaq, pre-market trading hours are 4:00 am to 9:30 am, Eastern Time Zone. After hours runs from 4:00 pm to 8:00 pm, Eastern Time Zone. Certain brokers have different pre-market and after hours trading times. Some online brokers do allow you to trade during those hours; check with your broker to see if you're eligible to make those kinds of trades. Know that Extended Markets carry risks. The volatility tends to be much higher, and there is less liquidity, meaning that fewer people are trading and that prices tend to move much more dramatically.
